newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah eases in late trade, swaps down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah eases in late trade, swaps down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was soft in late trading on Tuesday in face of continued ample liquidity and a stronger dollar against the Japanese yen and other major currencies, dealers said.
"The rupiah remained under pressure because of continued ample liquidity and a stronger dollar against other major currencies," one European bank dealer said
Spot rupiah was at 2,432.00/32.50 at 1005 GMT against an opening of 2,431.80/32.30.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were last at 2,432.00/32.50 and 2,433.00/33.50, respectively.
Another foreign bank dealer said reports on Indonesia's expected June consumer price index did not have much impact on the market as the figure was still within expectations.
Indonesia's consumer price index for June was likely to show a month-on-month fall of 0.16-0.18 percent, compared with a rise of 0.19 percent in May, government officials said on Tuesday.
Short-term swaps also remained under pressure from the strong dollar and sustained ample rupiah liquidity, dealers said.
One senior director with a U.S. bank in Jakarta said the falls in the rupiah short-dated swap rates were due to rising onshore dollar lending rates because of quarter and half-year end demand.
"As a result dealers who need to borrow US$ overnight and tom/next have been generating them by buying and selling US$ through the short-date swap market," the director said.
Overnight swap was last at -0.10/par from an opening of 0.15/0.30 while tom/next was down at -0.05/par against 0.10/0.20 at the opening.

One-month swaps also fell to 10.50/11.00 from an opening of 11.00/12.00, two fell to 22.50/24.00 from 25.50/26.50, three to 37.00/38.00 from 36.25/37.25 and six to 77.50/79.00 from 81.00/82.50 points.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, raised its intervention band by one point to 2,427/2,619 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,427/2,475 late on Tuesday.
